0.long_answer: The gene in question is PAX2, which is a member of the paired box (Pax) gene family. These genes encode transcription factors that play a crucial role in various developmental processes. Specifically, PAX2 is involved in the development and proliferation of multiple cell lines, the formation of organs, and the proper organization of the central nervous system. In the context of coloboma—a congenital malformation often linked to defects in eye development—abnormalities in PAX2 can disrupt these developmental processes, contributing to the occurrence of this birth defect. In developmental biology research, PAX2 has been shown to be essential in the regionalized embryological development of brain regions such as the midbrain and hindbrain, underscoring its importance in cell line development, organogenesis, and CNS organization.
